newsitem.title: GERMANY: Legal challenges to EMU will fail - Bonn deputy.
newsitem.headline: Legal challenges to EMU will fail - Bonn deputy.

text.p: A senior German member of parliament believes any attempts to challenge European economic and monetary union (EMU) will meet with failure, a German newspaper reported on Monday.

The business daily Handelsblatt quoted Ruprecht Scholz, a member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), as saying Germany's highest court had already examined the currency union and found it did not violate the constitution.
Scholz, a deputy parliamentary leader of the CDU, said he believed a complaint to the European court would also be fruitless.
He said the court would find no grounds for objection as long as the currency union conformed to the rules laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.

A Munich journalist, Klaus Peter Heim, has already filed a complaint with the Federal Constitutional Court, the first of several challenges expected to be made in Germany once the first wave of EMU members is decided next year.

Heim says he wants the court to reject EU decisions allowing what he calls "accounting tricks" by France and Italy to help them meet the Maastricht treaty's strict budget deficit target of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
